title: Recursive equations of the inverse coefficient transpose
statement: For l,E,D,o,d and rec as in [def-sf-integral-expression-recursion-data], let canonicalComparisons be the inverse explicit coefficient transpose [lem-sf-integral-expression-transpose-is-iso]. For every finite input index I, expression e with its geometric conditions, and K in its full input domain, Equations(d,canonicalComparisons,e,K) holds. This gives the leaf inverse-unit equation, unary and tensor counit-transport equations with their domain witnesses and invertible transport factors, and the open/proper expansion of compact support. It asserts no agreement with a separate direct comparison.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence; agent-formulated expression-tree refinement, lem-sf-integral-expression-recursion, proof steps 1--11.

proof.text: Prove the generic transport calculation: if an isomorphism b has coefficient map r_H composed with A(R(c inverse) followed by epsilon), then its inverse is B(c inverse) followed by the inverse primitive comparison and L A(epsilon). Apply the inverse adjunction hom-set equivalence to both maps. Naturality of the counit, the primitive transpose equation, and naturality of r make their images equal. Injectivity identifies the inverse maps; cancel the isomorphisms to get the claimed hom equation. The same calculation works on a product input category.

Transport Good across an isomorphism. Normalization is transported using naturality of the actual transition transformations and cancellation of evaluation isomorphisms. Keep the same four common bounds: each finite-level constructibility predicate is closed under isomorphisms by the triangulated constructibility theorem, cohomological support is transported through homology isomorphisms, and Tor amplitude through the existing isomorphism witnesses. Keep every origin and transition square, composing its evaluation isomorphism with the image of the given system isomorphism.

For a unary vertex, Reconstruction.limit gives constructibility at L M and Reconstruction.reduction gives its Good reduction. Reconstruction.counit makes epsilon_M invertible. Transport the parent Good condition backwards through A(epsilon_M), using the preceding Good-invariance argument, to obtain the remaining basicUnaryDomain clause. Apply the generic transport calculation with the child and parent components of canonicalComparisons, whose coefficient identities are canonicalComparisons_coefficient; unaryTranspose supplies its primitive equation. Both factors of unaryA are isomorphisms. This proves the root equation and invertibility clause for pull, proper push and open extension; use the child induction hypothesis for the recursive clause.

At a leaf explicitly unfold only the transpose and coefficient transformation: the latter is identity, so the component is the actual unit. Reconstruction.unit makes it invertible, and the canonical hom is its inverse, equal to inverseOrZero. At tensor apply the generic calculation in the product input category, with the product of the two child comparisons and the pair of actual counits. The two limit/reduction witnesses and Good transport of the tensor of the counits give basicTensorDomain. tensorTranspose supplies the primitive equation, and the two child induction hypotheses give both recursive clauses. No distinctness of variables is used.

For compact support form the hidden finite-type compactification object over the base and its open and proper arrows. Apply the unary calculation to the explicit open expression on the same input family, whose domain witness is exactly the retained intermediate Good condition and the child admissibility. Apply it again to the proper step, using that open comparison as child comparison and the parent coefficient identity. Substitute the resulting open equation into the proper equation and pair with the original child induction hypothesis. This is literally the composite and the two domain witnesses required by Equations.

mathlib_searches.query: Adjunction transpose of a natural transformation is natural and satisfies the counit identity
mathlib_searches.results: Adjunction.counit_naturality, unit_naturality, right_triangle. These supply the formal adjunction calculation, but no expression-domain invertibility or geometric normalization theorem.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Generic adjunction tools only; specialized expression statement absent.

mathlib_searches.query: Natural isomorphisms for expression trees transported through an adjunction with invertible unit and counit
mathlib_searches.results: Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso, Equivalence.adjointifyη, Adjunction.unitAsIsoOfIso, conjugateIsoEquiv. No theorem for these full recursive intermediate domains.
Mathlib supplies Adjunction.homEquiv and its naturality; local rg finds only the assigned expression recursion and its downstream consumers, not a completed proof of the proposed steps.

lean.statement:
theorem canonicalComparisons_equations (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (o : Operations l E) (d : Primitives l E D o) (rec : Reconstruction l E D)
    {I : Type u} [Finite I] {X : I → Over (Spec (.of D.k))}
    {W : Over (Spec (.of D.k))} (e : Expression _ I X W) (g : e.geometric)
    (K : (e.domain l E o).FullSubcategory) :
    Equations l E d (canonicalComparisons l E D o d rec) e g K
